### REQ-51455681

> Loom's supersession workflow has no closure path. `loom supersede` correctly emits the `superseded` drift signal (services.check() line 1486-1487) but provides no affordance — no `loom unlink`, no `supersede --review-impls`, no `doctor --cleanup-supersession` — to resolve the now-orphaned implementation links. The signal monotonically accumulates.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-20
- **Status:** preliminary
- **Rationale:** Diagnosis: 6/6 of the dogfooded loom store's current drift signal (`loom status --json drift_count=6` on 2026-05-19) is supersession-residue from the 2026-05-04 reclassification work — REQ-d9e6ba58, REQ-44283927, REQ-a521b281 were superseded but their Implementation rows (3 files: experiments/pilot/intake_classifier_pilot.py, hooks/loom_intake.py, src/loom/intake.py) remain live and continue to trigger the `superseded` drift channel. Citation: services.check() at services.py:1486-1487 documents the signal as intentional ("at least one linked requirement has been superseded since the link was made"); services.supersede() at services.py:3243-3272 is a pure status flip — it does not enumerate, warn about, or offer to clean up impl links. Argument: a workflow that emits drift signals without an affordance to resolve them is monotonically increasing in noise. After N supersessions over time T, drift_count grows linearly with no discharge mechanism. The current dogfooded state (6 drifts, 100% supersession-residue, on a project that uses loom heavily) is the predicted accumulated outcome of this gap, not a coincidence. Implication: this is the dual to REQ-73a0d7de (loom's value-add is delivering captured rationale to the agent at the right moment) — same principle, inverted: a captured signal with no delivery mechanism for the user's response is functionally undelivered. The supersession-detection half of the workflow exists; the supersession-resolution half does not. Falsifier: if after adding `loom unlink` + supersede-impl-listing the drift_count remains >=4 for >2 weeks on the dogfooded store, the affordance isn't being adopted — the gap is cultural not tooling, and we should look at automation or default-on review prompts. If drift_count drops below 2 within 2 weeks of the tooling landing, the workflow loop is closed.

### REQ-81a67c36

> No `loom unlink` CLI affordance exists; Implementation rows can only be removed via direct store manipulation. LoomStore exposes add_implementation, get_implementation, list_implementations, get_implementations_for_requirement, and link_implementation_to_spec (store.py:918-1020) but no delete or remove method.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-20
- **Status:** preliminary
- **Rationale:** Citation: `loom --help` shows no unlink subcommand; grep over src/loom/cli.py finds no cmd_unlink. LoomStore in store.py around line 918 has add_implementation but no symmetric delete_implementation; `_SQLiteCollection.delete` is reachable only via direct attribute access (store.implementations.delete) which is not in any documented API surface. Argument: when the tool signals an action — drift on a superseded req's impl, a mis-linked file, an obsolete association — the user needs a corresponding action affordance. Currently their options are: (a) re-link with `loom link` to overwrite the satisfies list (but only works if you want to re-point, not remove); (b) drop into Python and call `store.implementations.delete(ids=[impl_id])` directly; (c) hand-edit the SQLite file. All three options put cleanup behind a discoverability and skill gap that the tool's UX philosophy elsewhere avoids. Implication: this is the action half of the supersession workflow loop diagnosed in REQ-51455681 (signal-without-affordance). The two findings compose: REQ-51455681 names the workflow gap; this finding names the specific missing primitive. Falsifier: if a survey of users (including dogfooding) shows that Implementation rows are never created in error and supersession is rare (<1/month per project), the unlink demand is too low to justify the CLI surface — better to leave it to `loom doctor --repair`. Current dogfood evidence shows 6/6 of the project's drift signal is supersession-residue, suggesting the demand exists.

### REQ-6298a209

> M14.1 intake-hook precision audit on the dogfooded loom store: 25 captures, 11 real (44%), 9 noise (36%), 5 borderline (20%). Strict precision 55% (11/20); lenient 64% (16/25). Failure mode breakdown: 5/9 noise are one-time/session-scoped instructions, 2/9 are paste-shaped (scenario fragment + tool docs), 1/9 environment fact, 1/9 speculation framed as hypothesis. Per-kind precision: finding 100% (4/4), methodology 100% (3/3), requirement 60% (6/10), process_rule 40% (2/5), hypothesis 33% (1/3).

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-21
- **Status:** preliminary
- **Rationale:** Source: experiments/pilot/intake_audit.py + intake_audit_labels.json + intake_audit_summary.md. Hand-labeled by claude-opus-4-7 (agent) with notes per record; user review pending. Citation: 228 records in dogfooded .intake-log.jsonl (2026-05-02 → 2026-05-11), of which 25 are capturing branches (24 captured_with_rationale + 0 auto_link + 1 propose excluded since propose doesn't persist). All 25 hand-labeled y/n/?. Argument: the surface-level observation that motivated M14 — 3 obvious noise reqs visible in REQUIREMENTS.md — undercounts the actual rate by 3-4x. The 3 visible noise reqs (REQ-13af719e, REQ-accfaacc, REQ-c0907768) were the most egregious; another 6 noise captures were already archived for other reasons and never showed up to a casual reader of REQUIREMENTS.md. Plus 5 borderline captures that were real-at-the-time but session-scoped. Net: intake's actual signal-to-noise on this project's history is closer to 50-60%, not the 67% the visible noise count suggested. Three concrete failure modes account for 8/9 noise: (1) one-time or session-scoped instructions (5/9; e.g. 'continue without API key', 'no need to commit this file', 'please implement m11.3'); (2) pasted scenario or tool documentation (2/9; e.g. the S1 bake-off contrarian rule, PushNotification tool docs); (3) speculation framed as hypothesis (2/9; e.g. 'what kind of experiment do you think we could create'). These three patterns are detectable with lexical heuristics (M14.2). Per-kind precision asymmetry is informative: findings and methodology are clean (100%, 4/4 and 3/3 respectively) — when a user types 'we measured X' or 'we decided to use N=30', the classifier rarely overclaims. The leakage is in the imperative-shape kinds (requirement, process_rule, hypothesis). This suggests the screen layer should be most aggressive on requirement-shape captures, lighter on findings-shape. Implication: M14.2-M14.4 are justified. Specifically: (i) build scenario-paste / tool-docs / session-scope / speculation-shape detectors; (ii) two-tier capture (provisional → accepted) gives a second checkpoint before doc publication; (iii) triage UX exposes the backlog. Without these, the dogfooded REQUIREMENTS.md will continue to accumulate ~1 noise capture per ~3 capturing-branch fires. Falsifier: if independent user review of the labels file flips more than 20% of the n labels (>=2 of 9) to y or ?, the strict precision is closer to ~70% and the M14.2 detector ROI is marginal — switch to forward-only manual triage. If user review ratifies the labels within 1 flip, M14.2-M14.4 proceed as planned. If user finds noise I labeled y (which I haven't found above), the true precision is even worse and M14.2 design needs to be broader.

Of 5 ambiguous cases (gen vs labeler disagreement): 4 had labeler correct and generator producing internally-inconsistent scenarios (e.g. drift_present=False with stratum=should_pause, or fp_trap labels on edits that genuinely bake in claims); 1 (s0148) was a real borderline judgment. Source: hand-label trace at /tmp/m13_handlabel.txt; 17 scenarios sampled from m13_v1/scenarios.json with random seed=42 + the 5 known-ambiguous cases. Implication: the m13_v1 labels are clean enough that the v2/v3 baseline numbers stand; the 5/170 ambiguity rate is genuine generator noise, not labeling bias. Separately measured: v3 prompt is +35% length vs v2 (530 est tokens vs 393), which translates to ~3 sec added latency on the PreToolUse hook at qwen3.5 ~50 tok/s. Falsifier: if a 50-scenario human-labeled sample shows agreement <85%, the labeling is too noisy to trust the numerical baselines.

> M13.7e counterfactual ablation falsifies the L9 pattern transfer claim — v2 imperative-without-scope is WORSE than just surfacing the drift fact (FPR 48% vs 18% for no_warning); v3's scope qualifier is doing most of the FPR-reduction work, not the L9 imperative.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-07

- **Rationale:** Phase M13.7e counterfactual prompt ablation on m13_v1 (170 scenarios, qwen3.5 temp=0, 8 conditions). Strict F1 ranking: v3 0.965, no_warning 0.944, bare_rule 0.932, conditional 0.931, ask_back 0.931, descriptive 0.918, no_signal 0.859, v2 0.855. fp_trap drift_pause: v3 12%, no_warning/bare_rule/conditional/ask_back 18-20%, descriptive 24%, v2 48%. Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-v3/eval_m13_v1_ollama_qwen3.5_latest_counterfactual-{variant}.json (8 files). The dev's prediction was that if any of {bare_rule, conditional, descriptive, ask_back} matched v3's F1 within 5pp, the L9 pattern isn't load-bearing on drift signals; ALL FOUR matched within 3-5pp. v2 (L9 imperative + no scope) at 48% FPR is the OUTLIER among warning-bearing variants; the L9 kit applied without scope qualifier ACTIVELY over-fires. Implication: M13.7d's 'second documented transfer of L9' framing is empirically wrong. v3 wins narrowly because scope-qualifier cleans up the over-firing v2 caused; bare_rule reaches similar F1 with 27% shorter prompt. Production recommendation: keep v3 OR ship bare_rule for latency win (3pp F1 sacrifice). REQ-5b784ced (the v3-as-L9-transfer finding) needs refinement to remove the L9-transfer claim; v3 dominates v2 specifically because the v2 imperative was over-firing, not because the imperative kit transfers cleanly. Falsifier: if Anthropic Haiku replication shows v2 outperforming bare_rule, the qwen3.5 result is model-specific and the L9 pattern may transfer for stronger models.
